title: C15 · The owner's screen, and the five questions it answers before you ask
anchor: Repository audit at commit ec37b81, 15 August 2026: 104 models, 68 pages, 229 routes, 41 dashboard sections. Live production read the same day.

slides.headline: FIVE QUESTIONS, ANSWERED BEFORE YOU ASK THEM
slides.sub: What the person who owns the shop can see without calling a meeting.
slides.boundary: Every screen shown in this document is the demo tenant.

slides.h2: WHAT AN OWNER ASKS ON A MONDAY

items.text: What is actually in the pipeline, not what somebody remembers
Which jobs are late, and who is waiting on whom
What closed this time last year and never came back
Which deals have gone quiet and nobody has admitted it
What my team did all week without asking them to report it

slides.boundary: Five questions that used to be five conversations.
Counted against live production on 15 August 2026, not estimated from the schema.

slides.quote: A feature only ships if it can fill its own fields. If it needs somebody to type, it lands at zero and stays there.
slides.src: The adoption law. It killed a nine week roadmap in one afternoon.
slides.boundary: Four of five recommended modules were rejected on this test alone.

left.p: A board full of open deals, half of them dead, nobody willing to be the one who closes somebody else's.

right.p: Still alive, nothing changed, dead, or too late. Every answer writes a real record. It is short and it is mandatory.

slides.boundary: The value of a clean pipeline is that the number at the top means something.

items.text: Insights, revenue and commissions over the same records the reps work in
Team settings, invite, suspend, reinstate, force a logout, reset a second factor
Admin control center, platform statistics, record merging, data export
Demo mode, a parallel empty database for showing the software to a prospect
Per client portal control, set the password, copy the link, switch it off

slides.boundary: A new hire is a database row now, not a deployment.

slides.label: of 17 recorded shipments. So the delivery risk engine says nothing rather than inventing a date.
slides.sub: One carrier is not entitled on the account, and the rate service cannot see roughly four in five of our shipments. That is an integration to buy, not a feature to fake.
slides.boundary: You will get told what it cannot see. That is the point of the tour.

head: Surface
State
slides.boundary: Maturity here is honest rather than promotional. The open items are on the page too.

slides.h2: WHAT I WILL TELL YOU FIRST
lede: The data richness comes from absorbing what your team already sends. A shop on a different system installs this and gets an empty database.
So the honest market today is narrow and specific, and the roadmap is one absorption adapter per system rather than more modules. I would rather say that out loud than sell you a pilot that starves.
slides.boundary: Said before the demo, not after the invoice.

lede: I will run it against your own channels and show you the fill rates on your own data before anybody signs anything.
slides.boundary: Phase one does not advance until partners beat their own baseline.
